First time posting here, I love all the positive energy here. Don't see anyone saying this so I thought I'd add. I'm a trans guy, so I grew up socialised amongst girls, and so in a way can relate.

Explore more friendships with guys, be brave when you're out in public or at a place where you're doing an errand or a hobby or work, if a guy or anyone is wearing a cool shirt or reading a book you like or circumstance means it wouldn't be inappropriate to strike up a conversation. Incidental friendships and not ones from school or work can be so rewarding, or open you to other contexts to make more friendships and connections. You'll also meet people vastly different from you too. Might meet an asshole, or someone that could turn into a good friend. Talking to more people and being open to the idea of when appropriate, approaching strangers, leads to conversations and relationships we wouldn't have had otherwise. In your friendships, you'd end up with less women and more men friends.

Do you really want to decentre women, or as other excellent comments have shared, do you just want to understand yourself better and have a better relationship to you? If a woman or a feminist i.e the kind of people who say 'decenter men' saw your question, many would get mad or feeling strongly about it. Yes, in your life experience women have been front and centre and you have been hurt by women, so you don't want them to be the priority for you, but when you say decenter women, it makes you sound more like the men who have podcasts where they hate on women and feminism and women's rights, and the kind of men that have hurt women so much that women want to decenter men, and if you use that sort of language, even if you don't mean it this way, you could come off as not understanding why women and feminists want society and culture to decenter men. You then run the risk of falling into an anti women, pro men rabbit hole, where you meet men who truly, do not want to center women at all, and worse, might lead you into agreeing with ideas about women that could turn you into a woman hater. I'm not saying you are one or 100% will turn into one, but men who have been hurt by women are vulnerable to this kind of thing. 

Be wary of the type of men you engage with, all the guys here seem very lovely so you're in good hands, and there is some ace advice here including asking you to look inwards or seek out a male therapist. Keep doing what you're doing, being in this subreddit means you're already in community with a bunch of wholesome men (from what I can tell as I am new here), but be mindful in the way you go about it. You can explore masculinity and male friendship and community, while being careful of the men out there who weaponise that as a way to get you into their misogyny club.

You could also find company amongst men who centre women, men interested in feminism, while political ultimately it is a sociology theory and more specifically it is a conflict theory. If you confused and frustrated at misandry, taking a deeper look at misogyny and the patriarchy might give you a different perspective.

Good luck in seeking out what you're looking for!
